memory_candidates.content: When adding deterministic logic that a skill's prose needs to call AND that must be unit-testable, expose it as a standalone bash script with pure, single-purpose subcommands (e.g. `script.sh normalize`, `script.sh tally-op`) that each read only their explicit args/files and print JSON to stdout. This lets a bash-assertion test file exercise each function in isolation via subshell command substitution, and lets skill prose document a stable CLI contract instead of inlining shell logic. Used for .claude/scripts/email-preference-harvest.sh (7 subcommands) and its test .claude/tests/test-email-preference-harvest.sh (35 assertions, all pure command substitution + jq).

check-extension-docs.sh's check_deployed_script_drift rule requires any script declared in an extension's manifest.provides.scripts to be byte-identical between the deployed copy (.claude/scripts/<name>) and the extension's own source copy (.claude/extensions/<ext>/scripts/<name>). When creating or editing such a shared script, always cp the deployed copy over the extension-source copy (or vice versa) before running check-extension-docs.sh, or the doc-lint FAILs with 'deployed script content drift'. Confirmed via memory-retrieve.sh (owned by core) and the new email-preference-harvest.sh (owned by email).

For a memory vault topic namespace meant for programmatic/aggregated writes (not free-text /learn segments), the reserved-namespace pattern is: (1) an exact topic== match short-circuits skill-memory's fuzzy classification straight to UPDATE/EXTEND, since the identity key is already deterministic; (2) memory-retrieve.sh gets a topic-prefix map(select(...)) exclusion so the namespace never leaks into general auto-retrieval; (3) /distill's zero-retrieval penalty AND purge OR-condition both get a topic-prefix exemption, since a low retrieval_count is expected (not staleness) when general auto-retrieval deliberately never selects the namespace. Implemented for email/preferences/* in task 822; reusable for any future write-only, externally-keyed memory namespace.
